title: Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (BC28): Download Symbols from Global NuGet Sources (without any environment)
summary: Business Central 2026 wave 1 introduces a new AL command to download symbol files directly from Microsoft's public NuGet feeds without needing a running environment, supporting country/region-specific packages and custom feeds through VS Code settings.
key_points: A symbol file acts as the source code of an extension, letting an AL project reference tables, pages and codeunits from the base app or other extensions
The new AL: Download Symbols from Global Sources command gets app packages from Microsoft's public NuGet feeds, so no Docker container or sandbox is needed
al.symbolsCountryRegion sets the localization using two-letter ISO codes such as us or de, or w1 for worldwide; if it is not set, you are prompted during the download
Custom public NuGet v3 feeds without authentication can be added, and al.useOnlyCustomFeeds limits downloads to those feeds
The version to download is controlled by the application property in app.json
features: Download Symbols from Global Sources command

quotes.text: Previously, you had to have a running Docker container or a Sandbox environment just to click Download Symbols and start coding.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the key problem solved by this feature - eliminating environment dependencies for symbol downloads

quotes.text: A symbol file is essentially the source code for an extension.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies what symbols are and why developers need them when building AL projects

quotes.text: Country/region codes must follow ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or w1 for worldwide.
quotes.why_it_matters: Specifies the exact format required for symbol localization configuration
